svg.title: Zero rotation: how to draw common footprints at 0°
svg.desc: Drawn to scale, six footprints at their IPC-7351B zero rotation, each on solder mask. Parts that could be placed the wrong way round have a pin-1 or cathode mark; the chip and the SOT-23 don't need one. A 0603 chip resistor or capacitor lies horizontal, with no polarity mark, since it isn't polarized. A SOD-123 diode lies horizontal with the cathode on the left. A SOT-23 has pins 1 and 2 on the left, pin 1 at the top, and pin 3 on the right, with no mark, since its pad pattern only fits one way. An 8-pin SOIC has pins 1 to 4 down the left side with pin 1 at the upper left. A 16-pin QFN has pin 1 at the top of the left side. A BGA has ball A1 at the upper left. The cross at the center of each part is the point the placement (XY) file gives.

g.text: pins 1 to 4 down the left side
at the top of the left side
Ball A1 at the upper left
Drawn to scale. Dashed line: the part's outline.
White dot or K: pin-1 or cathode mark, only where the pads would fit either way.
Cross: the part's center, the point the XY file gives.
Rotation in the XY file is measured from this drawing.
IPC-7352 leaves the convention to each library standard.
